items.title: Newer Qwen models that also see pictures
items.text: Qwen 3.5 4B and 9B and Qwen 3.8 27B join the catalog. They answer first and think only when asked. Qwen 3.5 4B is the new small everyday pick: it got all 39 of our reasoning questions right, where Qwen 2.5 3B got 28.

items.title: Models read four times as much at once
items.text: Chat models start with up to a 32K context window where it fits, not 8K. A request that needs more gets more, and with Advanced mode on you can choose a model's window. Windows past 32K use a cache half the size, so they fit more computers.

items.title: Faster answers by guessing ahead
items.text: Models guess the next words and check several at once, with the same answers. Editing pasted code is 42% faster, and Qwen 2.5 32B and 14B come with a small draft model that made them about 1.9× and 1.6× as fast on a 24 GB graphics card.

items.title: Models bigger than your graphics card run
items.text: A model too big for the graphics card now runs partly on the processor instead of failing to load. Each model's fit says how well it will run on this computer, not just whether it fits.

items.title: Your coding agents and editors, on your own models
items.text: Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Aider, and editors such as Continue and Zed can use a model on your computer: toskarctl connect sets them up. Anthropic's Messages and OpenAI's Responses formats work too, and toskarctl chat chats in the terminal.

items.title: Web pages and files can't give your AI orders
items.text: Text that tells the AI what to do, on a web page, in a file, or in a tool's result, is left out before the model reads it. A 7B model followed such an instruction every time before; now it never does.

items.title: Questions about your life stay in the chat
items.text: A question such as "Where does my sister live?" is answered from your chat and its summary, never looked up on the web. Long chats summarized twice keep what was said early on.
